title: Synthesis of Sorting Kernels
problem: Optimal small-array sorting kernels are difficult to synthesize manually; prior work (AlphaDev) required massive computational resources and achieved only partial solutions for arrays of length 3-5.
motivation: Efficient sorting is a fundamental operation used ubiquitously in data processing and machine learning; finding provably optimal or near-optimal kernels improves performance across numerous applications.
method: The algorithm uses A* search—a technique that systematically tries different solutions while using heuristics to steer toward the best answers. To stay efficient, it employs two types of shortcuts: some guarantee it never skips the optimal solution, while others speed things up by pruning unpromising branches (even if they might contain an answer). For arrays of length 3, it exhaustively tries all correct sorting kernels; for larger arrays, it intelligently samples the best candidates. This approach runs about 100 times faster than prior work (AlphaDev) without requiring specialized hardware like TPU clusters.
key_novelty: The core idea is using A* search with specialized heuristics and pruning to find optimal sorting kernels on standard hardware, thereby establishing the theoretical minimum size these kernels must have.
contributions: A* search-based algorithm with optimality-preserving heuristics and non-optimality-preserving pruning cuts
Complete enumeration of all correct sorting kernels for length 3 with best-performer selection
Discovery of near-optimal kernels for larger lengths with established tight lower bound for length 4
baselines: other synthesis techniques (all inferior for lengths >3)
limitations: Scalability to practical array sizes not discussed; computational cost for lengths >5 not analyzed.
primary_theme: Efficient A* enumeration of optimal sorting kernels
